file_name: Nystrom DT - 2018 - Methods for Patient Centered Interface Design of Test Result Display in Online Portals.txt

barriers.description: The user testing portion had a low sample size which the authors identify as a primary limitation of their evaluation.
barriers.justification: A small participant pool constrained the team’s ability to rigorously evaluate and generalize findings, hindering the Evaluate designs and Manage user understanding workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Aside from a low sample size, the main limitation of the user testing portion of our evaluation is the lack of a homologous “stimuli” to test with participants.

barriers.description: The team implemented a semi-structured design process without a strict schedule for when to begin testing and making improvements, prioritizing speed over experimental rigor.
barriers.justification: This methodological choice limited the rigor of evaluations and the systematic timing of iterations, impeding Integrate feedback & iteration and Evaluate designs workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In the current study, we chose to implement a semi-structured design process that refrained from using a strict schedule to determine when to begin testing and making interface improvements during the design of the interface. This methodology increased the speed at which the interface could be produced at the cost of rigorous experimental design.

barriers.description: A large majority (71 percent) of testing participants had prior health-care work experience, producing a non-representative participant sample.
barriers.justification: This participant composition limited the designers’ ability to derive insights representative of typical patients, constraining the Manage user understanding and Facilitate user involvement workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: An additional limitation that may affect the generalizability of the results of this study is the large percentage (71 percent) of patients who had history of working in health care prior to participating in this study.

barriers.description: The team did not assess the impact of creating non-linear visual scales after equalizing biomarker ranges, leaving an untested design consequence.
barriers.justification: By not evaluating how non-linear scales affected patient perception, designers lacked evidence to inform further iteration and evaluation, hindering Evaluate designs and Integrate feedback & iteration workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: We did not make any attempt to assess the impact of these non-linear scales on patient perceptions.

barriers.description: The interface used red/green color schemes that were not tested with colorblind participants, potentially limiting accessibility for some users.
barriers.justification: Failure to include color-vision-impaired users in testing limited the designers’ ability to address the holistic experience and to evaluate accessibility-related design solutions, hindering Understand context of use and Evaluate designs workloads.
barriers.reference_excerpt: In addition, the use of red/green color schemes for the design of our interface could potentially limit the ease of using this interface for colorblind patients.
